outcome.answer:
Paper [1] directly addresses how efficient-attention modules shape hybrid architectures, analyzing scaling and mechanisms. It finds efficient-attention design mainly affects how fast long-context capability emerges, and that long-range retrieval is carried by full attention while efficient attention shapes the optimization trajectory, including the “Large-Window Laziness” effect where larger SWA windows can delay retrieval head formation in full-attention layers. It also proposes improving long-context performance by applying NoPE only to full-attention layers in a small-window SWA hybrid.

If you instead meant a hybrid architecture efficiently combining attention types for long-context reasoning, paper [2] introduces Ring-linear models that integrate linear attention and softmax attention to reduce I/O and computation overhead, and explores the ratio between the attention mechanisms to find an optimal structure. Paper [5] focuses on principled head-level hybrid design separating retrieval and positional heads using intervention metrics and instantiating a head-wise hybrid architecture.
